questions.q: After Big Toomai used Kala Nag's leg chain on a new elephant, what did he tie Kala Nag with instead?
choices: A loop of grass string
A thick rope of twisted hemp
A spare leather harness strap
The chain from Pudmini's leg
questions.evidence: slipped a loop of grass string round Kala Nag's leg

questions.q: What did Kala Nag do when Little Toomai ran after him calling, "Take me with you"?
choices: He trumpeted loudly to wake Big Toomai in the hut
He came back, lifted the boy onto his neck, and went on
He pushed the boy gently back toward the camp
He waited until the boy climbed up his tail
questions.evidence: put down his trunk, swung him up to his neck

questions.q: How did Kala Nag move through the forest as he climbed the first hill?
choices: Crashing and trumpeting so the wild herds would hear him
Slowly, stopping every few steps to eat the grass
Almost without a sound, drifting through like smoke
Following a wide, bright road through the trees
questions.evidence: drifting through the thick Garo forest as though it had been smoke

questions.q: "Kala Nag reached the crest of the ascent and stopped for a minute." What is the "crest of the ascent"?
choices: The edge of a river
The bottom of a steep valley
The top of the climb
A clearing in the forest
questions.evidence: reached the crest of the ascent

questions.q: Why did Little Toomai lie down close to Kala Nag's neck as they rushed down into the valley?
choices: So the wild elephants would not see a man riding
So a swinging bough would not sweep him off
So he could keep warm in the cold night mist
So he could whisper orders into the elephant's ear
questions.evidence: lest a swinging bough should sweep him to the ground

questions.q: After crossing the river, how could Little Toomai tell many elephants had just gone the same way?
choices: He could hear them all singing up ahead
A wide path of bent grass was still trying to stand up
Their footprints were full of fresh river water
He saw their torches moving between the trees
questions.evidence: the bent jungle-grass was trying to recover itself and stand up

questions.q: What was the ground of the hilltop clearing like?
choices: Soft and muddy, full of deep footprints
Covered with thick, sweet jungle grass
Trampled down as hard as a brick floor
Scattered with broken branches and nuts
questions.evidence: trampled down as hard as a brick floor

questions.q: Why did Little Toomai believe he was safe as long as he lay still on Kala Nag's neck?
choices: The wild elephants could not see in the dark
Kala Nag had promised to fight any elephant for him
Wild elephants do not drag a man off a tame elephant's neck
Petersen Sahib's hunters were hiding in the trees nearby
questions.evidence: a wild elephant does not reach up with his trunk and drag a man off the neck of a tame elephant

questions.q: Which elephant that Little Toomai knew came up the hillside with a broken chain?
choices: Pudmini, Petersen Sahib's pet
Hira Guj from the plains lines
The young calf with the blotch
The old tusker from the Keddah
questions.evidence: it was Pudmini, Petersen Sahib's pet elephant

questions.q: Toomai heard "the incessant flick and hissh of the great tails." What does "incessant" mean?
choices: Soft and gentle
Never stopping
Sharp and sudden
Far away
questions.evidence: the incessant flick and hissh of the great tails

questions.q: What was the elephants' "dance" really like?
choices: They spun in circles, holding each other's tails
They stamped their feet together like a great drum
They trumpeted songs to the moon one after another
They swayed in pairs while the calves ran between them
questions.evidence: The elephants were stamping all together now

questions.q: What made the booming of the dance stop?
choices: A sudden storm swept over the hills
Kala Nag trumpeted a warning to the herd
The first ray of morning light
The sound of Petersen Sahib's guns
questions.evidence: the booming stopped with the first ray

questions.q: Why did the clearing look bigger in the morning than it had at night?
choices: The moonlight had made it look smaller than it was
The elephants had stamped the grass and cane into hard earth
Kala Nag had carried Toomai to a different, larger clearing
The elephants had pulled up trees to make a fence
questions.evidence: The elephants had stamped out more room

questions.q: What happened when Little Toomai reached Petersen Sahib's camp?
choices: He fainted after crying out that he had seen the dance
He was scolded and sent straight back to his father
He fell asleep on Kala Nag's back and could not be woken
He ran to Petersen Sahib's tent to ask for his reward
questions.evidence: he slid off his neck in a dead faint

questions.q: What proof did Machua Appa find that the boy was telling the truth?
choices: Tusks left behind on the floor of the clearing
Little Toomai's torch dropped near the river
Seventy tracks and marks of Pudmini's leg-iron
Trees knocked down along the road to the camp
questions.evidence: I have counted seventy tracks crossing the river

questions.q: How did Big Toomai look at his son and Kala Nag when he found them again?
choices: As though he were tired of them both
As though he were afraid of them both
As though he were angry with them both
As though he did not know them at all
questions.evidence: he looked at them as though he were afraid of them both

questions.q: What new name did Machua Appa give Little Toomai at the feast?
choices: Machua Appa the Younger
Toomai of the Elephants
Toomai the Brave Tracker
Master of the Keddah
questions.evidence: This little one shall no more be called Little Toomai, but Toomai of the Elephants

questions.q: What is this part of the story mostly about?
choices: A boy who sees the elephants' secret dance and is honored for it
A boy who tames a wild tusker and rides it into the Keddah
An elephant who escapes the camp to rejoin his wild family
A hunter who finally finds the hidden elephant ball-room
questions.evidence: who had seen what never man had seen before
